{{Short description|Generalization of algebraic interior}}
In [[topology]], a branch of mathematics, the '''quasi-relative interior''' of a subset of a [[vector space]] is a refinement of the concept of the [[Interior (topology)|interior]].  Formally, if <math>X</math> is a [[Vector space|linear space]] then the quasi-relative interior of <math>A \subseteq X</math> is
<math display=block>\operatorname{qri}(A) := \left\{x \in A : \operatorname{\overline{cone}}(A - x) \text{ is a linear subspace}\right\} </math>
where <math>\operatorname{\overline{cone}}(\cdot)</math> denotes the [[Closure (topology)|closure]] of the [[conic hull]].{{sfn|Zălinescu|2002|pp=2-3}}

Let <math>X</math> be a [[Normed space|normed]] vector space. If <math>C \subseteq X</math> is a [[Convex set|convex]] [[finite-dimensional]] set then <math>\operatorname{qri}(C) = \operatorname{ri}(C)</math> such that <math>\operatorname{ri}</math> is the [[relative interior]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Partially finite convex programming, Part I: Quasi relative interiors and duality theory|last1=Borwein|first1=J.M.|last2=Lewis|first2=A.S.|journal=Mathematical Programming|volume=57|year=1992|issue=1–3 |pages=15–48|url=https://legacy.orie.cornell.edu/~aslewis/publications/92-partially-I.pdf|access-date=October 19, 2011|doi=10.1007/bf01581072}}</ref>
